title: Full-Stack Development
headline: Build the interface. Own the application.
intro: Build complete web applications, from an engaging interface to APIs and data. Explore MEAN, MERN and Python-based development within one Full-Stack Development program, with a technology path shaped around your learning goals.
audience: College students, graduates and developers changing stacks
bridge: Beginners build web and programming foundations first. Working developers can use the readiness exercise to focus on unfamiliar layers, integration and production habits.
scope: One program, multiple technology paths. Build with Angular or React on the frontend, and explore Node.js/Express, Python/FastAPI, .NET or Java on the backend. Put the shared foundations into practice through a focused project in your chosen stack. The learning path and project depth are agreed for the learner or group.
paths: Connect an Angular interface to Node.js and Express APIs with MongoDB. Build confidence across the complete JavaScript/TypeScript application.
Build a React interface, connect Node.js and Express APIs, and model application data in MongoDB. Follow the same end-to-end engineering progression.
Explore Python/FastAPI, ASP.NET Core or Java/Spring Boot as backend paths. Connect an Angular or React frontend to clear API contracts and suitable application data storage.

modules.title: Web & programming foundations
modules.summary: Understand the browser, the network and the language behind the interface.
topics: Semantic HTML and responsive CSS
JavaScript variables, functions, arrays and async code
TypeScript types and errors
HTTP, JSON, Git and debugging
tools: Browser developer tools — inspect requests and layout
JavaScript + TypeScript — application logic
Git — versioned changes
VS Code — editing and debugging
modules.practice: Build a responsive event-information page and a small interactive registration preview using sample data.
criteria: Forms have labels and keyboard access
Layouts work on small screens
Errors can be reproduced and explained

modules.title: Interface design, accessibility & responsive layouts
modules.summary: Build interfaces people can understand and operate across devices.
topics: Semantic HTML and meaningful page structure
Responsive grids, typography and content hierarchy
Labels, validation messages, keyboard focus and status feedback
Loading, empty, success and failure states
Reusable components and design tokens
tools: HTML and CSS — create resilient responsive layouts
Browser accessibility tools — inspect names, roles and focus
Angular templates or React components — connect application state to clear feedback
modules.practice: Design a course-search and application flow at mobile and desktop widths. Include an empty result, invalid form, slow request and successful submission without relying on colour alone.
deliverables: Responsive interface and reusable component inventory
Documented loading, empty and error states
criteria: Complete the core task with a keyboard
Keep text and controls usable at 320 pixels
Preserve entered values after recoverable validation errors

modules.title: Frontend application development: Angular & React
modules.summary: Compose a maintainable interface with real application states.
topics: Component design with Angular templates or React JSX
Routing, forms and reusable interface patterns
Dependency injection in Angular; props, hooks and composition in React
HTTP integration and loading, empty, error and permission states
tools: Angular — components, routing, forms and dependency injection
React — components, props, hooks and composition
TypeScript — typed application models
Browser developer tools — network and runtime diagnosis
modules.practice: Build a searchable opportunities interface with detail pages, validated forms and clearly differentiated loading and error states.
deliverables: Frontend application in the chosen Angular or React path
criteria: Routes can be opened directly
Invalid form input receives useful feedback
The interface handles slow or failed requests

modules.title: State, asynchronous flows & client performance
modules.summary: Keep the screen consistent when requests are slow, repeated or cancelled.
topics: Component state, shared state and clear ownership
Angular signals and observable streams; React state, effects and shared-state patterns
Debounced search and cancelling obsolete requests
Route loading, caching boundaries and stale data
Profiling rendering, bundle size and network requests
tools: Angular signals — model local and shared reactive state
RxJS — compose and cancel asynchronous streams
React hooks — manage state and synchronise with external systems
Browser performance and network panels — inspect bottlenecks
modules.practice: Build searchable paginated results with loading feedback. Delay responses so older requests finish last and verify that the latest search still controls the screen.
criteria: Prevent stale responses from replacing newer results
Clean up subscriptions, effects and repeated event handlers
Explain caching choices and invalidation behaviour

modules.title: Node.js, Express & API contracts
modules.summary: Build the service behind the user experience.
topics: Node.js runtime and asynchronous I/O
Express routes, middleware and validation
REST contracts, pagination and consistent errors
Configuration, secrets and integration tests
tools: Node.js + Express — HTTP service
TypeScript — request/response types
OpenAPI — documented contracts
API test client — inspect boundary cases
modules.practice: Create an opportunities API with pagination, validation and a simulated unavailable dependency. Connect it to the chosen Angular or React frontend.
criteria: Server validation does not trust the browser
Errors avoid leaking internal details
Pagination and failure paths are tested

modules.title: MongoDB, identity & secure workflows
modules.summary: Connect data and permissions to the application’s business rules.
topics: Document modelling and relationships
Indexes, query patterns and update consistency
Authentication versus authorisation
Role checks, input safety and audit needs
tools: MongoDB — document storage and indexing
Express middleware — enforce access rules
Test fixtures — roles and permission cases
Git — review schema and API changes
modules.practice: Add owner and reviewer roles to a sample request-management workflow. Enforce permissions on the server and investigate a slow query.
criteria: Changing a browser value cannot grant access
Indexes serve the demonstrated query patterns
Sensitive fields are not returned unnecessarily

modules.title: Data modelling, queries & consistency
modules.summary: Choose data structures around real reads, updates and constraints.
topics: MongoDB embedding versus references
Schema validation, indexes and query inspection
Pagination and bounded result sets
Atomic updates, transaction boundaries and repeated requests
Relational modelling and migrations in the Python backend path
tools: MongoDB — model document relationships and inspect queries
MongoDB Compass — explore sample data and indexes
PostgreSQL — compare relational constraints in the Python stream
modules.practice: Model users, projects and applications for a sample opportunities portal. Compare two document designs, add an index for a frequent query and handle a repeated application safely.
deliverables: Data model and example access patterns
criteria: Tie each index to an actual query
Avoid unbounded data reads and growing embedded arrays
Explain which consistency guarantees the chosen operation provides

modules.title: Authentication, authorisation & integration boundaries
modules.summary: Connect accounts and external services without trusting the browser.
topics: Authentication versus permission to act
Sessions, cookies and token lifecycle concepts
Object-level access checks and role boundaries
Input validation, output handling and safe database queries
External API timeouts, retries and server-side configuration
tools: Express middleware — enforce permissions on server routes
FastAPI dependencies — illustrate equivalent checks in the Python path
A test identity provider or fixtures — practise login without real credentials
HTTP test clients — exercise unauthorised and repeated requests
modules.practice: Add member and reviewer roles to a sample request workflow. Attempt to access another user’s record, replay a request and call an unavailable service; make the server enforce each boundary.
criteria: Treat hidden UI controls as convenience, not authorisation
Keep secrets out of bundles and version control
Avoid duplicate side effects during retry

modules.title: Python, .NET & Java backend paths
modules.summary: Explore backend choices while keeping the application contract clear.
topics: Python functions, modules and exceptions
FastAPI request validation and SQL persistence
Relational modelling with PostgreSQL
Integration patterns for ASP.NET Core and Spring Boot
tools: Python + FastAPI + Pydantic — typed backend path
PostgreSQL — relational application data
pytest — Python service tests
ASP.NET Core / Spring Boot — .NET and Java backend paths
modules.practice: Build an equivalent API feature in the chosen Python, .NET or Java path and connect an Angular or React frontend. Compare request validation, persistence and setup while keeping the user journey consistent.
deliverables: Backend service-integration exercise in the chosen path
criteria: The client contract remains explicit
Credentials stay server-side
Explain the chosen stack and the transferable patterns across backend options

modules.title: Testing, release & portfolio delivery
modules.summary: Finish with an application that another developer can run and review.
topics: Unit, integration and browser-flow testing
Accessibility and responsive checks
Containers, configuration and release basics
Logging, rollback, documentation and demonstrations
tools: Browser automation — verify a complete user journey
Docker — repeatable setup
Git — reviewed release and README
Chosen backend test tools — regression coverage
modules.practice: Deliver a complete application in the agreed stream. Rehearse invalid input, denied access and a database outage before presenting the normal workflow.
criteria: Another learner can run the application
No secrets are committed
The demo includes failures and known limitations

projects.title: Campus opportunities portal
projects.problem: Students need a clear way to discover events or opportunities and view relevant details.
projects.practice: Build search, filtering, routing and responsive pages with sample opportunities. Work from a user story to an Angular or React screen, Express route and MongoDB collection. Include search, pagination, validation and an empty state. Test a repeated application and make the interface explain what happened. Keep example users and opportunities clearly fictional.

projects.title: Role-based request manager
projects.problem: A team needs request submission, review and status visibility with clear permissions.
projects.practice: Build the workflow in the chosen stream, including validation, status transitions and a permission matrix. Define a permission matrix before adding roles to the interface. Implement checks on the server, then attempt cross-user reads, unauthorised transitions and repeated operations. Show the reviewer queue, approval decision and user-facing receipt with predictable error recovery.

projects.title: A deployable full-stack product
projects.problem: A coherent application needs reliable setup and a clear engineering story.
projects.practice: Integrate the portfolio features, document tradeoffs and rehearse deployment locally with containers. Prepare environment configuration, a repeatable build and a deployment checklist. Rehearse an unavailable dependency and show useful logs without exposing personal details or secrets. For the Python path, document the equivalent API contract; other backend variants depend on the agreed stream.

preparation: Trace a browser action from an accessible Angular or React interface through validation, API logic, permissions and database access, then back to useful loading, success and failure states.

Use JavaScript/TypeScript and Python exercises to explain arrays, maps, complexity and debugging. Use arrays, strings, hash maps, searching and complexity analysis in practical exercises. Add a debugging walkthrough that separates a browser state problem from a server or database problem.

Present your MEAN, MERN or chosen backend project. Explain frontend composition, API contracts, data modelling, authentication, testing and deployment decisions. Connect what you built to the shared practices across technology stacks.

Demonstrate a working app, useful commits, tests, accessible UI states and a reproducible README. Prepare a setup guide, architecture diagram, API examples, automated checks and a short demo. Include one meaningful tradeoff, a known limitation and the next change you would make.
curriculumTitle: Full-Stack Development curriculum: understand the whole application.
curriculumIntro: Explore ten modules spanning web foundations, Angular or React interfaces, Node.js and Express APIs, MongoDB and relational data, authentication, validation, testing and deployment. Apply these skills through MEAN, MERN or a Python, .NET or Java backend path.
